# Results — Study 802 (Stock-Split-Modern)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**the classic positive post-split drift (Ikenberry-Rankine-Stice 1996) still exists in
the post-2020 mega-cap era**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint
`f41f9d523e91` (the forward-split event calendar).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | `yfinance` split calendar + total-return (`auto_adjust=True`) daily closes for a 30-name large-cap basket **and SPY** (5,406 rows, 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30) |
| Events | **44 forward splits** (ratio ≥ 1.5) with a usable 3-month window, effective dates 2010-08-24 → 2025-11-17; **19 pre-2020, 25 post-2020, of which 7 are mega-cap** (TSLA/NVDA/AMZN/GOOGL/AAPL) |
| Measure | **market-adjusted abnormal CAR** = stock buy-and-hold − SPY buy-and-hold over the identical window; entry at the ex-date close (first earned return t+1, the single documented lag); horizons 21/63/126/252 trading days + a [−1, +1] around-ex window |
| Statistics | Newey-West (Bartlett) HAC one-sample *t* on the **date-ordered** abnormal CARs (decisive); plain one-sample *t*; Welch *t* of the pre/post-2020 difference; Wilson interval on win rate; random-non-split-date placebo |
| Adjustment | **total-return** (dividends + splits folded in) throughout; every CAR is **market-adjusted** (SPY-hedged) |

**Survivorship / selection is named on the Signal axis:** the basket is a
*current-membership* list of today's large-caps — a selection of names that already won,
a bias that points **for** the drift. A failure to find positive drift *even here* is a
strong `NONE`, and the bias cannot be blamed for the absence.

## The headline — market-adjusted abnormal 3-month CAR by cohort

| cohort | n | mean CAR | median | HAC *t* | plain *t* | win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| all forward splits 2010+ | 44 | **−1.83%** | −2.65% | **−0.82** | −0.91 | 45% |
| pre-2020 | 19 | +3.37% | +2.44% | +1.48 | +1.29 | 63% |
| **post-2020 (modern)** | 25 | **−5.78%** | −5.45% | **−2.21** | −2.12 | 32% |
| post-2020 **mega-cap** | 7 | −4.95% | −5.45% | **−0.77** | −0.77 | 43% |

The claimed **positive** drift is nowhere: across all 44 splits since 2010 the abnormal
3-month CAR is **−1.83% (HAC *t* = −0.82)**. The pre-2020 slice at least has the *right
sign* (+3.37%) but cannot certify on this basket (*t* = +1.48 < 2). In the post-2020 era
the sign **flips negative** (−5.78%, *t* = −2.21), and the **Welch *t* of the pre→post
difference is −2.42** — a real regime change away from the anomaly.

## The near-term dip is horizon-fragile — modern (post-2020) cohort

| horizon | n | mean abnormal CAR | std | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m (21d) | 25 | −3.69% | 7.62% | **−2.27** |
| 3m (63d) | 25 | −5.78% | 13.62% | **−2.21** |
| 6m (126d) | 25 | −2.58% | 21.83% | −0.76 |
| 12m (252d) | 24 | **+5.44%** | 32.70% | +0.97 |

The post-2020 underperformance is a **near-term** effect (significant at 1m and 3m) that
**evaporates by 6 months and turns positive by 12 months** — the exact opposite of a
persistent drift. Around the ex-date itself ([−1, +1]) the modern cohort is a flat
**+0.46% (*t* = +0.66)**: no ex-date pop either.

## The seven headline mega-cap splits — tiny N, huge idiosyncratic spread

| ticker | ex-date | ratio | raw 3m | abnormal 3m | abnormal 12m |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| TSLA | 2020-08-31 | 5:1 | +13.9% | +9.8% | +16.4% |
| AAPL | 2020-08-31 | 4:1 | −7.6% | −11.6% | −12.8% |
| NVDA | 2021-07-20 | 4:1 | +19.4% | +15.3% | +2.9% |
| AMZN | 2022-06-06 | 20:1 | +1.1% | +5.8% | −8.2% |
| GOOGL | 2022-07-18 | 20:1 | −11.4% | −5.5% | −9.2% |
| TSLA | 2022-08-25 | 3:1 | −38.1% | −34.4% | −26.6% |
| NVDA | 2024-06-10 | 10:1 | −11.2% | −14.0% | +5.0% |

Seven events, a **+15% to −34%** abnormal-3m spread, mean **−4.95% at HAC *t* = −0.77** —
statistically indistinguishable from zero, and dominated by the single Tesla-Aug-2022
event (−34%). This is the study's core point: the mega-cap "split magic" is a handful of
high-beta names whose signs cancel; there is no signal to speak of.

## Placebo — random non-split entry dates, same names (post-2020, 3m)

Observed split-cohort abnormal mean **−5.78%** vs a random-non-split-date basket mean
**+4.81%** (sd 3.95%) over 1,500 draws → **p = 0.999**. Entering these names on their
split date was *worse* than entering on a random date — a mild "sell-the-news", the
opposite of the claimed buy signal.

## The timer — buy the ex-date close, hold 3 months, long-only, SPY-hedged

Modern cohort; 25 events over ~15 years ≈ **1.6 events/yr**. One round trip = 2 × one-way
cost × NAV.

| cost (one-way) | gross/event | net/event | one-sample *t* (net) | Sharpe | worst single event |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | −5.78% | **−5.88%** | −2.16 | −0.55 | −34.5% |
| 20 bps | −5.78% | −6.18% | −2.27 | −0.58 | −34.8% |

The long timer *loses* money (the modern edge is negative); the implied **short** timer
would have to borrow high-beta mega-caps and eat a −34% single-event tail, on 1.6 events a
year — un-scalable and un-investable. On the seven actual mega-caps the long timer nets
**−5.05% at *t* = −0.78** — nothing. **Tradability = MIRAGE.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic raw stock + market price paths with synthetic split dates and a TUNABLE
planted **abnormal** post-split drift; flows through the *same* market-adjusted panel; no
network.

| world | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (planted = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **+0.45** (sd 0.79), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/12 seeds** |
| planted +8 bps/day abnormal (seed 802) | **+4.05** (mean CAR +8.57%) |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up cleanly on a planted drift. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The classic *positive* post-split drift is absent on the real tape:
  all 44 splits since 2010 average −1.83% abnormal at 3m (HAC *t* = −0.82); even the
  pre-2020 slice, with the right sign (+3.37%), fails to certify (*t* = +1.48). No cohort
  clears **t ≥ 2 positive**. The post-2020 sign flips negative (Welch difference *t* =
  −2.42), so if anything the anomaly *reversed*.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** ~1.6 events/yr; the modern long timer loses (−5.88% net,
  *t* = −2.16); the seven headline mega-caps net −5.05% at *t* = −0.77; one Tesla-2022
  event (−34%) drives the mean; the short leg is un-borrowable/un-scalable.
- **"Is the near-term dip a real inverse signal?" — BUSTED.** The post-2020 −5.78% at 3m
  clears \|*t*\| = 2 and the placebo agrees (*p* = 0.999), but it is **horizon-fragile**
  (gone by 6m, +5.44% by 12m) and **vanishes on the seven actual mega-caps**
  (*t* = −0.77) — a tiny-N, selection-biased "sell-the-news" blip, not a robust
  tradable inverse drift.
